BREAKING: Taiwan announces new restrictions on short selling after its stock market falls -18% in one week, its worst weekly decline in 35 years.

Effective Monday, regulators will ban short sales below the previous closing price and raise margin requirements to 150%.

Taiwan’s $15 billion stock stabilization fund has also been buying shares to support the market.

Authorities are intervening to contain selling pressure.

BREAKING: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries fell -$76 billion in September, to $9.24 trillion, the lowest since October 2025.

This also marks the 3rd monthly decline over the last 4 months, down -$246 billion since February.

Japan, the largest foreign holder, cut its holdings by -$5 billion in September, to $1.06 trillion, its lowest since December 2024.

The UK, the 2nd-largest holder, reduced its holdings by -$9 billion, to $986 billion, its 3rd-highest on record.

At the same time, China, the 3rd-largest holder, slashed its holdings by -$27 billion, to $564 billion, its lowest since July 2008.

Foreign demand for US Treasuries is weakening.

US stocks have rarely been this oversold:

The S&P 500 closed the week 4.1 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, its widest deviation since August 2015.

This also marks its 3rd-largest deviation in at least 20 years.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, the index’s largest deviation from its 50-DMA was 3.6 standard deviations.

Not even the 2020 Pandemic crash saw such extreme oversold conditions, with the S&P 500 falling 3.8 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average in February.

During the 2022 bear market and the April 2025 post-"Liberation Day" selloff, the S&P 500 fell 3.2 and 3.3 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, respectively.

This has been one of the sharpest market sell-offs in history.

Market sentiment has taken a complete 180 degree turn:

The Fear & Greed Index fell to 9.7 points on Friday, below 10.0 for the first time since March 2026.

This marks its 4th lowest level since the 2022 bear market.

A reading below 30.0 indicates "Extreme Fear" territory and oversold market conditions.

The index has fallen -30.6 points, or -76%, over the last 6 trading sessions, its sharpest decline since February 2025.

The last 3 times the Fear & Greed Index fell below 10.0, the S&P 500 rallied +10.5% on average over the next 3 weeks.

Since 2021, the S&P 500 has gained +9.0% on average over the 3 weeks following readings below 10.0.

Sentiment is extremely polarized right now.

Inflation in Japan is accelerating:

Japan's CPI inflation excluding fresh food jumped +2.1% YoY in September, its highest YoY increase since December 2025.

Since May, Japan's CPI inflation has risen +0.6 percentage points.

Furthermore, CPI excluding fresh food and energy surged +2.4% YoY, its largest YoY increase since January.

Overall CPI inflation rose +2.1% YoY last month, its highest reading since November 2025.

This comes as the Iran War continues to fuel inflationary pressures in Japan, which relies heavily on imported food and energy.

Meanwhile, Japan's major food and beverage companies planned price increases for 3,153 items in October, the 2nd consecutive monthly reading above 3,000 for the first time since July 2023.

Inflationary pressures in Japan are broadening again.

BREAKING: The US Economic Surprise Index is up to 71 points, its 2nd-highest reading since August 2023.

This metric compares actual economic data with market expectations, rising above 0 when data beats estimates and falling below 0 when data misses expectations.

Excluding July and August 2023, this is the highest reading since the rapid economic recovery following the 2020 Pandemic.

Since August, the index has surged +56 points, or +373%.

Over the last 23 years, the index has exceeded its current level only 5% of the time.

The US economy is gaining momentum.
What is dead may never die.

BREAKING: This past week's -10.4% drop in the Nasdaq 100 was one of the rarest weekly declines in 40 years.

Of the last 2,133 trading weeks, just 11 saw declines of this magnitude or worse.

That's 0.52% of all weeks, a 3.27 standard deviation move based on the historical mean and volatility.

Of course, market returns exhibit "fat tails," meaning extreme moves occur more frequently than a normal distribution would predict.

However, even accounting for the fact that extreme market moves are more common than traditional statistical models suggest, this was a historically rare selloff.

Volatility returns when markets least expect it.

Investor positioning in copper is cratering:

Speculative investors sold -$1.3 billion in Comex copper futures in the week ending November 10th, marking the 7th consecutive weekly sale.

This group includes hedge funds, commodity trading advisers (CTAs), and other institutional investors.

Since September 22nd, they have sold a cumulative -$10.8 billion.

This brings long speculative investor positioning down to ~$5.2 billion, its lowest since October 2025.

Meanwhile, copper futures fell -5.3% on Wednesday, marking their largest daily decline since July 2026.

Copper prices are now down -18.2% from their September peak, to $5.67 per pound, their lowest level since April.

The copper market is seeing a massive shift in sentiment.

The semiconductor trade is still popular among fund managers:

39% of global fund managers said "long global semiconductors" was the most crowded trade, according to a BofA survey of 169 fund managers overseeing $461 billion in assets conducted between November 6th and November 12th.

This marks the 6th consecutive month that semiconductors have held the top spot.

However, this figure is down from the 82% peak recorded in July this year.

Meanwhile, “Short China Stocks” ranked 2nd for the first time, with 14% of respondents identifying it as the most crowded trade.

By comparison, "Long Magnificent 7" and "Short Treasuries" were considered the most crowded trades just by 12% and 10% of fund managers, respectively.

Investor appetite for semiconductor stocks remains strong.
